turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and a call at 4:40. Owen's zero went into the gradebook and he read it on his phone in the middle of class. Who decided that, and why didn't anyone call me first?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
Okay. And what did you find in them? I'm not interested in what you reread, I'm interested in what you have in your hand that I can read myself.
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked who decided on the zero, and why nobody called me before it went in. Answer that.
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why does he have a zero? I'm writing down that you said that, Hale. Now, who decided?
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
It only becomes a fight when my question goes unanswered. Third time, Hale: who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before they did?
